rules.title: Gateway CA Expiring
rules.subject: gateway
rules.fires: The CA each appliance reports holding, under 30 days (negative: expired).
rules.description: The CA each appliance reports holding, under 30 days (negative: expired). The threshold is the delay. NoData is a fleet with no appliances.

rules.title: Service Token Expiring
rules.subject: service_identity
rules.fires: A machine identity's token past its warn point, 7 days before expiry or a quarter of a shorter lifetime.
rules.description: A machine identity's token past its warn point, 7 days before expiry or a quarter of a shorter lifetime. The query emits only those, so any row is the alert. One instance per token; it clears when the token is revoked, its identity withdrawn, or it expires.

SELECT collected_at        AS "time",
       identity_name       AS identity,
       principal_id::text  AS principal_id,
       jti                 AS jti,
       renewal             AS renewal,
       to_char(expires_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI "UTC"') AS expires_at,
       remaining_seconds   AS remaining_seconds
  FROM public.service_token_health
 WHERE warn_at <= collected_at

After that the API refuses it, and the client using it stops working. {{ if eq $labels.renewal "keys_rotate" }}The deployment reads this key at start: run npm run keys:rotate to sign new keys and put them in place, then revoke the old token on Access Control, under Machine identities.{{ else }}Issue a new token for {{ $labels.identity }} on Access Control, under Machine identities, put it in the client, then revoke the old one.{{ end }}

rules.summary: The log store is refusing lines ({{ $labels.reason }}) and they are being lost. This is a ceiling in loki/loki.yaml doing its job: `rate_limited` is ingestion_rate_mb, and `stream_limited` is max_streams_per_user -- which usually means a label was promoted that should have stayed a field. Raise the bound or fix the cause; do not ignore it.

rules.description: The forward's retries or losses, or lines handed to it and none sent, either protocol, for 15m. Zero while observability.alloy.logForward is off.

(sum(rate(loki_write_batch_retries_total{component_id="loki.write.forward"}[10m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(loki_write_dropped_entries_total{component_id="loki.write.forward"}[10m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(otelcol_exporter_send_failed_log_records_total{component_id="otelcol.exporter.otlphttp.forward"}[10m])) or vector(0)) + (sum(rate(otelcol_exporter_enqueue_failed_log_records_total{component_id="otelcol.exporter.otlphttp.forward"}[10m])) or vector(0)) + ((sum(rate(loki_relabel_entries_written{component_id="loki.relabel.forward"}[10m])) > bool 0)

       or sum(rate(otelcol_exporter_sent_log_records_total{component_id="otelcol.exporter.otlphttp.forward"}[10m]))
       or vector(0)) == bool 0)
   or vector(0))

rules.title: Database Connections Near Limit
rules.subject: platform
rules.fires: Over 80% of max_connections for 5m.

Find what is holding them open (the Backends by State panel separates `idle in transaction` from `active`) before raising max_connections.

rules.title: Database Deadlocks
rules.subject: platform
rules.fires: Any deadlock in 10m.
rules.description: Any deadlock in 10m. The window is the delay, so `for: 0s`.
rules.summary: {{ $labels.job }} has recorded {{ $values.B }} deadlock(s) in the last ten minutes. PostgreSQL resolved each by killing one transaction, so the database is healthy and an application saw an error it may not have logged. Two transactions are taking the same locks in different orders.

rules.title: Transaction ID Wraparound Approaching
rules.subject: platform
rules.fires: age(datfrozenxid) over 1e9.
rules.description: age(datfrozenxid) over 1e9. A TRANSACTION count, whatever the metric's _seconds suffix says; do not turn the threshold into a duration.
rules.summary: {{ $labels.job }} has a transaction ID age of {{ $values.B }} (TRANSACTIONS, not seconds). PostgreSQL refuses all writes at about 2.147e9 and recovers only in single-user mode. Autovacuum is being prevented from freezing -- look for a long-lived transaction or an inactive replication slot, then let autovacuum catch up.

rules.title: Historian Policy Job Failing
rules.subject: platform
rules.fires: failures_total rising within 1h.
rules.description: failures_total rising within 1h. On the failure count, not last_run_succeeded, which is 0 for a job that has never run.

queries.text: sum by (job_id, proc_name) (increase(aber_historian_job_failures_total[1h])) and on (job_id) aber_historian_job_runs_total

rules.summary: TimescaleDB job {{ $labels.job_id }} ({{ $labels.proc_name }}) has failed {{ $values.B }} time(s) in the last hour. Retention, compression and rollup refresh are what keep the historian's storage and its aggregates true; a failing policy has no other symptom until the volume fills or a dashboard quietly goes stale. Check the job's last error: SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.job_stats WHERE job_id = {{ $labels.job_id }};

rules.summary: {{ $labels.job }} has not answered its own exporter for five minutes. The exporter runs beside the server in the same pod and connects over loopback, so this is the database itself: down, still recovering, or out of connections. Nothing reaches it either -- check the pod: kubectl -n aber logs {{ $labels.job }}-0 -c {{ $labels.job }}

rules.title: Database Collector Failing

The exporter is still serving and the scrape still succeeds, so every panel and rule built on that collector's series is now silently empty rather than reporting a problem. Usually a missing extension or a privilege the exporter's role does not hold -- kubectl -n aber logs {{ $labels.job }}-0 -c metrics names the cause.
